title: No phase transition guards — any phase can be reached from any other
evidence: handleAnalyze calls setPhase('scanning') unconditionally, then schedules 4 setTimeout chains: t1→results(2s), t2→battle(20s), t3→compare(58s), t4→cta(76s). Catch block → setPhase('landing'). No guard checks current phase before transitioning. No assertion that data/battleData/compareData exists before their phases render.
rationale: Timer-based transitions have no guard conditions. If a fetch fails silently, the phase advances but data stays null, producing blank screens. The landing→scanning→results chain is reliable because the API always returns data in demo mode, but the roast/compare phases depend on separate fetch calls that can fail.
fix_guidance: Add guard: before setPhase('battle'), verify battleData is non-null. Before setPhase('compare'), verify compareData is non-null. For failed fetches, show error phase or retry instead of silently advancing to blank state.

title: Loading guard releases too early — ANALYZE button re-enabled mid-flow
evidence: finally { setLoading(false); } fires immediately after fetch resolves (~2ms). But the 76-second phase sequence is still running. The ANALYZE button becomes clickable again mid-battle/mid-compare. WalletInput.tsx line 71: button disabled checks `!addresses.trim()` (empty check) plus `isLoading`, so while the button enables, submitting while data is mid-flow causes re-entry.
rationale: setLoading(false) fires after the fetch resolves, not after all phases complete. A user clicking ANALYZE again during the battle phase would trigger a new fetch, overwriting existing timers without clearing old ones, and resetting all state.
fix_guidance: Add isAnalyzing state that stays true until phase reaches 'cta' or error. Or use phase !== 'landing' && phase !== 'cta' as the disable condition instead of loading.

title: Phase renders with null data — battle/compare phases show blank screens on fetch failure
evidence: page.tsx:173: `{phase === 'battle' && battleData && (<RoastBattle battle={battleData} />)}` — if battleData is null, the battle phase renders a completely blank Terminal. Same for compare at line 174. Error in roast fetch at line 34: `.catch(() => setPhase('battle'))` — sets phase but NOT battleData, which stays null. The RoastBattle.tsx component's auto-advance timers (line 13-19) fire regardless — on null battleData, currentLine is undefined → 'Cannot read properties of undefined' error.
rationale: Fetch failures at /api/roast or /api/compare produce 38 seconds of blank screen during the battle phase. The user sees 'Battle complete' status text but no content. The RoastBattle component crashes trying to access undefined properties on null battleData.
fix_guidance: Add explicit null/error state handling: if fetch fails, show error message and skip to next phase. Or add an 'error' phase. At minimum, guard RoastBattle render with proper null checks on nested properties.

title: Fetches can fail silently — no dead-end recovery path exists
evidence: Line 34: `fetch('/api/roast').then(r=>r.json()).then(d=>{setBattleData(d.battle);setPhase('battle')}).catch(()=>setPhase('battle'))`. If the fetch succeeds but d.battle is undefined (malformed response), setBattleData stores undefined, then setPhase('battle') renders null-guarded blank screen. If fetch fails entirely, catch sets phase to 'battle' with null battleData — blank screen for 38s. Same pattern for /api/compare at line 35. No way for user to recover — they must refresh.
rationale: Both roast and compare fetches have the same error pattern: catch sets phase but not data, leaving the user stuck viewing nothing for the duration of that phase's timer window (38s for battle, 18s for compare). The only recovery is browser refresh.
fix_guidance: On fetch failure: show inline error message with retry button. Or skip to next phase immediately. Add 'Error' button/text overlay during blank phases.

title: Timer overwrite on re-entry — old timers fire after new sequence starts
evidence: Line 37: `phaseTimers.current = [t1, t2, t3, t4]` directly overwrites the ref array without calling clearTimeout on old timers first. Line 26 cleanup only fires on component unmount (useEffect return), not on re-entry. If a user clicks ANALYZE during an existing flow (made possible by check 2.2's premature loading release), old timers keep firing after new timers are set — potentially calling setPhase for old phases that conflict with new ones.
rationale: Mid-flow re-entry orphans the old setTimeout handles. The cleanup only runs on unmount (useEffect return), not on handleAnalyze re-entry. Old timers continue firing, producing race conditions between old and new phase transitions. React StrictMode in development would double-mount and double-fire timers, though this is dev-only.
fix_guidance: Before setting new timers: `phaseTimers.current.forEach(clearTimeout)`. Add a guard at the top of handleAnalyze: `if (phase !== 'landing' && phase !== 'cta') return;` to prevent re-entry.
